capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the abscissa statement, compare the absolute Dirichlet series of the Möbius coefficients with the zeta series:

- Since \(\mu(n)\in\{-1,0,1\}\), its complex cast has norm at most \(1\). Thus the series converges absolutely whenever \(\Re(s)>1\), giving abscissa \(\le 1\).
- At every prime \(p\), \(\mu(p)=-1\), so the absolute series at \(s=1\) contains \(\sum_p 1/p\), which diverges. Hence it does not converge absolutely at \(1\), giving abscissa \(\ge 1\).

Translate these two facts through the characterization of `LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv`.

For the `primesBelow` identity, use `Finset.ext` and split on `Nat.Prime n`. Membership in `Nat.primesBelow (n + 1)` means “prime and \(p<n+1\),” and the elementary equivalence
\[
p<n+1 \iff p<n\ \lor\ p=n
\]
shows that the new finset is `insert n (Nat.primesBelow n)` exactly when \(n\) is prime, and is unchanged otherwise. Combine the two independently proved components with `And.intro`.
